absent: Locking discipline for standard resources, per-CPU SDEI state, and hook registrations.
Numeric encodings for relocation flags, page size, alignment limits, and hypervisor call numbers.
Full realm_config layout, RSI call numbers, and complete error code set.
SDEI event dispatch, masking, and completion protocol beyond entry selection.
Device tree and ACPI parsing internals, memblock handling, and page table creation.
CPU operations table contents and secondary processor boot sequence.
Interactions with address sanitizer, randomization, firmware interfaces, power-state methods, and early console.

findings.text: Relocation entry receives a kimage descriptor and transfers control to a staged kernel after copying its pages, handling translation teardown and selecting hypervisor versus direct entry based on recorded vectors and device tree location.
Descriptor fields must be captured before any page movement because the descriptor itself can be overwritten, and data plus instruction coherence must complete before translation is disabled.
Walk state pairs a remaining depth counter with a slot for the chosen caller address.
Depth query adds two to skip its own frames, walks the current thread, and returns either the selected caller address or null when the stack is shallower than requested.
Per-frame callback consumes one depth unit while positive and only stores the current location once the counter reaches zero, using its boolean result to continue or stop the walk.
Realm support keeps one static configuration record and one global protection attribute used to distinguish shared mappings.
Realm availability is advertised by a static key that starts disabled and is enabled only after full initialization succeeds.
Version negotiation accepts only the compiled interface level, treats explicit lack of support as absence, and otherwise requires exact success before proceeding.
Memory protection pass must convert every usable range and halts boot on any failure because subsequent access would fault unrecoverably, while destroyed pages must never become RAM.
Remap hook classifies each physical range as protected or not and selects encrypted versus decrypted page attributes accordingly while always succeeding.

Realm initialization proceeds only with monitor transport and compatible version, then loads configuration, derives the shared protection bit from IPA width, registers remap and encryption hooks, protects memory, and finally marks presence.
Shared protection attribute encodes the bit below the configured address width translated into page table format.
Protection hook registration allows a single owner and reports busy with a warning if called again.
Memory encryption operations registration allows a single owner and reports busy with a warning if called again.
Realm encryption setup forwards its fixed operations table to the generic single-owner registration.
Dummy platform device object carries a fixed device name with no instance number.
Late creation registers the dummy device solely when running in realm world and only logs on registration failure.
Diagnostic lines from the SDEI file use a fixed short subsystem prefix.
Global exit selector records which calling convention completes an event, hypervisor or monitor.
Each processor has independent pointers for normal and critical event stacks, independent shadow stack pointers, and independent current event records for both priorities.
Event stack provisioning allocates one virtual stack per possible processor for each priority and on any allocation failure releases all prior allocations before reporting lack of memory.
Shadow stack provisioning is bypassed when the feature is off and otherwise follows the same per-processor allocate with full cleanup on failure pattern using its own allocator.

Entry point resolution rejects certain hypervisor boot configurations, ensures event and shadow stacks exist, remembers the conduit choice, and returns either a trampoline alias when the kernel is hidden from user space or the direct handler, with zero signalling failure after cleanup.
Early resource pair describes kernel text and data as system RAM with bounds initially zero and later patched from link symbols.
Standard resource count and array start empty and are sized from the firmware memory region count during claiming.
Firmware boot arguments occupy four aligned 64-bit slots with the trailing three required to be zero.
Primary processor setup extracts the hardware identifier from identifier registers, records it for logical zero, and announces the boot processor.
Processor identity comparison is equality between a supplied hardware value and the stored logical mapping.
Logical mapping holds one hardware identifier per possible processor prefilled with an invalid sentinel, while the hash record stores per-level shifts together with mask and total width.
Affinity hash discovery keeps only bits that vary across processors, compresses each level into a dense index, and warns when the resulting bucket count is disproportionately large.
Machine description setup reserves the firmware blob, spins without fault recovery when it is absent or malformed, otherwise reprotects it read-only and records the model name.
Temporary device tree mapping requires a non-zero minimally aligned address, validates magic and size ceiling after mapping the first page, and extends the mapping when the blob spans pages.
Early mapping helper rejects virtual addresses below the kernel base and otherwise creates a non-allocating page table entry.
Resource claiming publishes kernel text and data extents then creates one entry per firmware memory region, marking non-mapped regions as reserved memory and others as busy system RAM.
Reservation pass clips firmware reserved extents against each standard resource with page rounding and carves overlaps as reserved children.

Architecture bring-up orders early address space, firmware blob, static keys, parameters, exception masks, identity teardown, firmware interfaces, memory and paging, table parsing, resource claiming, power-state and realm setup, and SMP identity before checking boot argument compliance.
Secondary enumeration selects firmware table source, aborts without a valid boot processor, respects disabled SMP, clips surplus cores, and discards entries whose setup fails.
Per-processor setup demands successful operation binding and initialization before marking the processor possible.
ACPI processor discovery enumerates interrupt controller entries for processor records then associates each logical processor with its node.
Without ACPI SMP support the discovery routine is an empty operation.
Absent processors are denoted by a distinguished invalid hardware identifier value in the logical map.
Non-zero trailing boot arguments are reported as a bootloader violation without stopping boot.
Misaligned kernel base and translation already enabled at entry are reported as firmware defects with warning and taint respectively.
